summary: Stripe Apps require OAuth 2.0 with PKCE support using S256. Developers use the CLI to create, configure, and upload apps. Public distribution requires an account activation, adherence to strict manifest guidelines, and a formal review process that takes approximately four business days.

reason.text: The process involves using the Stripe CLI to create an app, configuring the manifest with specific OAuth settings, and registering redirect URLs.

blockers.issue: Consuming an authorization code more than once revokes the account connection.

claim.text: Consuming an authorization code more than once revokes the account connection.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Per OAuth v2, this endpoint isn’t idempotent. Consuming an authorization code more than once revokes the account connection.

blockers.fix: Remove localhost or dummy URLs before uploading your app.

claim.text: The app manifest must not contain localhost or dummy URLs for redirect URIs.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: The app manifest field allowed_redirect_uris must not contain localhost or dummy URLs. These entries pose a significant security risk and can enable unauthorised redirects.

blockers.fix: Disable MFA or provide instructions to bypass it.

claim.text: Test credentials provided for review must not require multi-factor authentication.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Disable multi-factor authentication or provide instructions for reviewers to pass it.

blockers.issue: Do not include custom cryptographic functions in your app code.
blockers.fix: Always use cryptographic functions provided by standard libraries or well-established open source libraries that have been properly vetted.

claim.text: Do not include custom cryptographic functions in your app code.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Your app code must comply with all applicable export control laws. Specifically, don’t include any custom cryptographic functions in your app. Custom cryptography is subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), and exporting such code outside the United States can result in severe penalties.

blockers.issue: Do not publish the same app under different names or categories.
blockers.fix: Submit new versions of an app from the same account as the previous version.

claim.text: Do not publish the same app under different names or categories.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Don’t publish the same app under different names or categories. Submit new versions of an app from the same account as the previous version.

blockers.issue: You cannot set a public distribution for another app if you already have a public app in…
blockers.fix: Change the distribution type from private to public only if there are no other public apps within the same Stripe account.

claim.text: You cannot set a public distribution for another app if you already have a public app in the same account.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: After you upload an app with a public distribution, you can’t set a public distribution for another app within the same Stripe account.

blockers.issue: Publicly distributed apps cannot contain specific restricted words in their names.
blockers.fix: Remove the banned words from your app name in the manifest and upload a new version.

claim.text: Publicly distributed apps cannot contain specific restricted words in their names.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: Beginning in September 2024, Stripe apps with a public distribution type can’t contain the words “Stripe”, “app”, “free” or “paid” in their names.

blockers.fix: Contact Stripe Support at least 6 weeks in advance.

claim.text: If you request a large limit increase, you must contact Stripe Support at least 6 weeks in advance.
claim.label: official_docs
claim.evidence_quote: If you request a large increase, contact Stripe Support at least 6 weeks in advance.

blockers.issue: Making changes after submitting an app for review will restart the review process.
blockers.fix: Ensure all information is accurate before submitting the app for approval.

claim.text: Making changes after submitting an app for review will restart the review process.

response_type
